codec.description: How the bytes read: a Limitless `StorageBufferMsg` or an Omi ring record

index.description: The phone's store index: the flash life times 2^40 plus the device's own index

startMs.description: Capture placement, epoch ms; left out for an Omi record (the server places it from its stamp)

droppedMessages.description: Pendant messages the phone dropped since launch: a malformed fragment or one that didn't decode.

timeZone.description: The phone's time zone, "Europe/Berlin": the owner's days and times follow it.

intelligence.description: Seconds from a chapter's end to its summary

PendantStatus.description: The Pendant as the phone last saw it; null before any heartbeat

Heartbeat.description: The phone's last heartbeat; null before any

mac.description: The Mac helper, live or as it last left

binaries.description: Every binary in the call stacks: the app's UUIDs are its dSYMs'.

build.description: The build and OS the diagnostic was recorded on.

objcException.description: Never the composed message or its arguments.

durationSeconds.description: A hang's duration, or a CPU exception's CPU time.

count.description: Repeats within the hour, sent again under the same id.

metrics.description: A day of MetricKit metrics, numbers only: seconds, bytes, counts.

truncated.description: The phone dropped frames past its cap.

id.description: The phone's; a retried event is stored once.

days.description: The last 30 local days, oldest first, today last.

elevenLabsThisMonth.description: Speech-to-text ElevenLabs itself reports this month for the whole workspace (every key and app). Null when it didn't answer.

claude-code.description: Always 0: the Mac runs on the Max plan.

codex.description: Always 0: the Mac runs on the ChatGPT plan.

unpricedRuns.description: Runs on a model with no known price: not in usd.

usd.description: Estimated from tokens at list prices.

hours.description: Billable hours at the base rate, keyterms included.

jobId.description: The job its block became; null while open

highestPage.description: The highest page index stored, null when none is: a hint, not a resume cursor (holes stay below it)

labeledUntil.description: Capture time up to which the server has labeled the source's speech, null before any

page.description: The first index that holds other bytes: the phone moves it and the pages after it to a new band

TimedWords.description: Each word: start and end in ms from the passage's start, and its UTF-16 length in the text with the spacing before it (none before the first)

id.description: Stable: a re-summarized chapter keeps it

cursor.description: The last seq read: pass it as `since` next time

durationSeconds.description: Seconds of speech audio the job holds

endedOnSilence.description: True: no speech for at least 30 s after its audio, so no turn follows it closely. False: closed at 2 minutes or on a 5 s pause, whatever followed. Null on older jobs

more.description: Ask again at once with the new cursor

firstPage.description: A withdrawn job or speech fragment's first page: the phone sends its pages again

removed.description: Rows that no longer exist (a turn moved off its map, a person merged away, a job's last speaker row, unsent audio withdrawn): drop them

vocabulary.description: The owner's words, whole on every page

closed.description: Settled: the source heard on 5 minutes past its end (an imported one always), so grouping adds nothing to it; late audio or an edit can still reopen it

endEdit.description: The live split its end comes from: what Undo undoes

place.description: Apple's name of its most accurate named fix

retired.description: Out of the live set (merged or undone): drop what was built from it

runId.description: The summary its title, TLDR and chapters come from: Generate's `after`

splitSuggestions.description: Where the latest summary would split it, unsure: the owner splits there or dismisses it

startEdit.description: The live split its start comes from (in the gap before it, or at it), else the merge that joined it: what Undo undoes

state.description: Where it stands (conversation-state.ts); the phone adds only Not uploaded yet

able.description: Summaries run on the Mac now; otherwise they wait for it

reason.description: Why the Mac can't, for 10 minutes after it said so. auth: the selected CLI is signed out on the Mac; limit: the selected subscription's usage limit. Null: away, asleep, or able

asleep.description: The Mac was going to sleep: nothing could be dictated to it from then on

heardAt.description: When the server last heard from the Mac

watchedThrough.description: Every dictation before this is already a quiet range: now while the Mac's socket is open and nothing is pending, else the last time it was heard

ai.description: Summaries and titles on the Mac, off by default. Off: they wait

engine.description: Which subscription runs AI on the Mac: Claude Max or ChatGPT Codex

openAppAfterMinutes.description: Minutes the Pendant's audio may wait on the phone, while it records, before a notification asks the owner to open the app. 0: never

transcriber.description: Who transcribes the next blocks: ElevenLabs Scribe whole, or the speech service with Scribe for the Thai turns (docs/processing.md). Speech without the speech service set up (IDENTITY_URL) still goes to Scribe

transcription.description: Audio to ElevenLabs and voices to speaker recognition. Off: uploads wait unsent

conversationId.description: The live conversation its start falls in: the server's placement, the one rule

displayName.description: What every reader calls it: the person's name, else "Speaker N" in its conversation, as the summaries do

personName.description: As emitted; a rename comes in `people`

text.description: Without dictation and media: empty when all of it is hidden

source.description: The dictating app's bundle id, or "playback" from the phone

parts.description: The jobs whose turns start inside it, in order, with their time maps

mode.description: rolling for every run since Oct 14; the others are older

result.description: Turn ids index into turns. Kept even when invalid. From prompt version 4, chapters come first and each chapter's summary is its own call; boundarySuggestions are only strong ones, each with a cause (people, call, place or silence) and, from prompt version 7, a confidence: high is an AI split, medium is offered for the owner to split at or dismiss. From prompt version 8, chapter summaries and the TLDR write speakers as tokens like {S2}; speakerTokens says which voices each stands for, to render with the name the transcript gives them.

starts.description: Where each segment begins in the job's audio (ms), when the server joined it from speech fragments; absent, each begins one separator after the one before

placeName.description: Apple's name for where it was taken (a street or a district, and the city)

place.description: The phone's name for the place, when it has one

exact.description: The passage contains the query as typed.

dateRange.description: Capture time of the passage's start: from inclusive, to exclusive.

people.description: Person ids: passages where one of them speaks.

terms.description: The owner's words, sent as keyterms before people's names and aliases

heardThrough.description: Capture time of the durable, analyzed, contiguous page prefix; only moves forward

sentThrough.description: Every kept second before it is in a speech fragment the server holds: the start of the first stretch not sent, or heard-through when none waits. The server closes blocks on it

audible.description: Some analyzer but Silero heard sound

breaks.description: Why this span starts apart from the one before (`missingPages`, `untimedPage`, …), at its start

speech.description: Speech as segmentation counts it (uncertain audio included)

unanalyzed.description: Audio no analyzer reached yet, pieces of a second or more

post.description: The phone's capture health: at most every 6 h while the app runs, at once on each change of the Pendant's connection or recording, and on notable events. Idempotent by id. Kept 90 days.

put.description: The app's push token (hex), for silent pushes and alerts such as the morning's voices to name. Sent by the app's sync runs until this server has it; replaces the one before.

get.description: How capture and processing are doing, for the owner's own sessions: the archive's invariants, the Pendant and phone as last reported, the Mac helper, the backups, ElevenLabs' credits and latency, where audio and summaries are (`pipeline`), and the last day's problems and chain steps. It scans the last day: call it on demand, poll `/status/live`. Spending is not here.

The cheap part of `/status`, for the Mac host's menu, polled every 30 s: the pipeline, the backups, speaker recognition, the Mac, the Pendant and phone as last reported, ElevenLabs' credits and the switches. The device token only.

post.description: One MetricKit diagnostic (crash, hang, CPU or disk-write exception) or a day of metrics. Idempotent by id. Kept 90 days.

get.description: Diagnostics received since `since`, newest first, or the one with `id`.

post.description: One step the phone saw in a chain the owner relies on (a push, playback kept quiet, the cutover). Ids, states and counts only. Idempotent by id. Kept 14 days with the server's own.

get.description: The server's and the phone's events since `since`: the latest `limit`, oldest first.
A job's parsed transcript; a turn's index in `turns` is its `turnIndex`.
What was spent, from our own ledgers at list prices: today, the last 30 days and this month (days in the owner's time zone), split by service.

post.description: ElevenLabs transcription webhook. Verified with ElevenLabs-Signature over the raw body.

get.description: The pages the server holds of a source: every job's, any state, and every speech fragment's in no job. The phone sends kept speech from every other page. `jobId` is the job's or the fragment's id, read only by the phone build of Oct 15. `handedOver`: whether the cutover happened; a reinstalled phone starts its cursor from this only then. `sentThrough`: the source's phone's last word, everything before it sent or decided; a new install starts its cursor at the page holding it.

put.description: Upload one speech fragment: the kept speech of a run of whole Pendant pages the server doesn't hold, as Ogg Opus, with its pages and map. The server checks the hash, the Ogg duration (1 s tolerance) and that the map fits the audio, and keeps it in the bucket until it closes the fragment's block itself (on its own clock, the phone's `sentThrough`, or 2 minutes of speech). Idempotent: the same pages and audio answer the same fragment; any 2xx means the pages are with the server. Refused with 409 `held`, nothing kept, when a job or another fragment holds any of its pages: the phone reads `GET /sources/{sourceId}/blocks` and renders again without them. When its block closes, a fragment bought already (or from before the Mac's quiet ranges) is covered, its pages held and nothing sent; one a quiet range touches is withdrawn, and the feed lists it as a removed job with its first page: its pages are the phone's to send again.

400.description: Invalid metadata, audio hash mismatch, or audio that is not Ogg Opus of the declared duration or its map

409.description: Some of its pages are held already (held): nothing was kept

503.description: The audio could not be stored (audio_store_unavailable): nothing was kept

get.description: What the server holds of a source's raw pages.

put.description: Upload raw pages exactly as the phone stored them, contiguous from `firstPage`, in index order. Idempotent: a page already stored with the same bytes is accepted and kept once. Any 200 means every page of the batch is with the server. The server decides what gets transcribed: it labels the speech of an Omi source's pages and cuts it into speech fragments itself, as the iPhone would.

400.description: Invalid metadata, a hash mismatch, lengths that don't add up, or pages not contiguous from firstPage

409.description: A page's index holds other bytes (page_conflict), as after a new flash life the phone didn't band: nothing was kept

503.description: The pages could not be stored (audio_store_unavailable): nothing was kept

post.description: Transcribes the audio before a press of the Pendant's button at once, with the blocks' keyterms, and answers its words. Nothing of it is stored but what it cost. Refused while transcription is off (409).

400.description: Audio that is not Ogg Opus of at most 2 minutes

put.description: The prepared Ogg Opus of a completed job whose audio the bucket lacks, re-rendered by the phone from its packs (the render is deterministic, so the hash matches). Refused with 409 audio_hash_mismatch unless its sha256 is the job's audioSha256, and 400 invalid_audio unless it lasts the job's duration (1 s tolerance). Stored under the job's key (`jobs/<sha256>.ogg`) and recorded on the job; idempotent. Nothing is admitted, sent or billed. Also for imported old-app recordings: their jobs exist with their sha.

200.description: The audio is in the bucket

400.description: Not Ogg Opus of the job's duration

409.description: The hash is not the job's, or the job is not completed

put.description: A sealed raw pack, content-addressed (`raw/<sourceId>/<name>-<sha256>.pack`), at most 64 MB, with its hash in `X-Content-Sha256`. It holds everything the Pendant heard, dictation included: stored, never processed. Idempotent: one already held answers `stored: false`.

200.description: Held; `stored` is false when it already was

400.description: The body does not hash to X-Content-Sha256

put.description: A snapshot of the phone's source.sqlite (the receipts that tell how to read the packs), at most 64 MB, hash in `X-Content-Sha256`. One per UTC date is kept, the last 7 dates; idempotent for the same bytes.

200.description: Held; `stored` is false when it already was

400.description: The body does not hash to X-Content-Sha256

get.description: What the server holds of this source's raw backup: each pack's name, hash and size, and the newest source.sqlite snapshot. The phone uploads only what is missing.
The Ogg Opus audio of a job, as kept in the bucket: the file a queue clip's `audio` points into (seconds from its start). Honors one `Range: bytes=` header. 404 for a job from before the bucket.

200.description: The audio, or the range asked for (206)

put.description: The owner names (kind new), assigns (kind person) or un-assigns (kind unknown) a speaker, or one turn when turnIndex is set. Evidence from that scope in this transcript moves with it. Survives every later recognition run. A new person takes the id the phone chose, so a replay makes nobody twice.

patch.description: Rename a person or set the other names they go by (the whole list). Evidence and assignments are untouched.

post.description: Merge personId into {id}: its evidence and assignments move over, then it is deleted; its names become aliases. A replay, once personId is gone, answers {id} as it is.

get.description: The voices to name: unnamed voices of the last 30 days that talked with the owner (at least 10 turns traded and a minute of talk), one item per voice across conversations and days, the most back-and-forth first, each with clean clips of its voice and the name the summaries heard or who it sounds like.

post.description: The owner's answer for a queue item's voices: a new person (name), a person (personId), nobody they know (ignore), a video or TV playing (media), or several people (several: who; each turn is decided among them), then the rest of their turns as they read (rest). Each voice becomes the owner's correction of that speaker, so voice evidence moves with it; answered voices leave the queue.

200.description: The person the voices went to

get.description: What this voice source offers a reader (docs/voice-source.md): the contract's version and its optional parts. A reader's token may still not open every one.

The feed (docs/voice-source.md): `since` a decimal seq (none or 0 for everything); up to 500 changes after it, each row as it is now. `wait` holds the request up to that many seconds while nothing is newer (an empty page with the same cursor at the end).

post.description: A stretch to leave out of transcription, from the phone (its device token): `source` "playback" while it plays a recording out loud. (The Mac's dictation ranges come on its socket.) Words already bought inside it are hidden. Idempotent by id: a retry returns the range as stored.

get.description: One conversation: its range, titles, latest run and jobs.

put.description: Set (or clear, with null) the owner's title. It always wins over generated titles and no regeneration overwrites it. Between edits, the latest by editedAt wins.

editedAt.description: When the owner made the edit, on the device that did; now when omitted. A time in the future counts as now. An edit older than the stored one is ignored.

200.description: The conversation, with the title that won

post.description: The owner's Generate: the title, TLDR, chapters and boundary suggestions again. `after` is the summary he saw (the feed's `runId`, null for none): when a run newer than it is already valid, running or waiting, nothing happens and it answers 200 with that run, so a replay asks nothing twice. Otherwise it is summarized again from its first turn, window after window, on the Mac (the owner's subscription); with the Mac away it waits for it. The summary shown stays until a newer run is valid. Answers 202 with the latest run as it stands; read the feed for the rest. Never on a paid API.

200.description: A run newer than `after`: nothing asked

202.description: Generating: the latest run as it stands, if any

post.description: The phone's whole location history: every fix it took, with Apple's place name when it has one, and every visit iOS reported. The server names conversations' places from it. Idempotent: one fix per instant (a name sent later fills one stored without); a visit is keyed by its arrival (its departure when iOS didn't see it arrive) and replaced when sent again with its departure.

200.description: Rows written; a fix already stored as it is counts 0

get.description: Where the owner was at an instant: the stay around it, or the nearest point within 30 minutes, else nothing. A day's stays: `GET /visits` with its `from` and `to`.

Each stay, newest first, at most 200: every one, or those at the place the phone named (`place`, matched in part), or by `latitude` and `longitude` within `radiusM` (100 m). `from` and `to` bound it (a day: the reader's own bounds of it); the whole history without them.

404.description: No place the phone named matches

post.description: Passages (about 30 to 60 s of turns) ranked by meaning and by the passages holding every word typed, the two rankings fused, best first: a passage both find outranks one only one finds; by words alone while the embedder is down. Embedded on the Mac (docs/providers.md). Conversations are indexed in the background after each change.

put.description: Turns transcription or AI on or off, picks who transcribes, or sets when the app asks to be opened. Turned back on, what waited goes on: the phone is nudged to send its waiting audio, summaries due run on the Mac.

ai.description: Summaries and titles on the Mac, off by default. Off: they wait

engine.description: Which subscription runs AI on the Mac: Claude Max or ChatGPT Codex

openAppAfterMinutes.description: Minutes the Pendant's audio may wait on the phone, while it records, before a notification asks the owner to open the app. 0: never

transcriber.description: Who transcribes the next blocks: ElevenLabs Scribe whole, or the speech service with Scribe for the Thai turns (docs/processing.md). Speech without the speech service set up (IDENTITY_URL) still goes to Scribe

transcription.description: Audio to ElevenLabs and voices to speaker recognition. Off: uploads wait unsent

put.description: Replaces the owner's words with this list (idempotent); the feed carries them (`vocabulary`). Blocks uploaded from then on are transcribed with them; nothing is transcribed again.

The phone's timeline facts for a source, by span. A span replaces the stored one with the same first page; heard-through only moves forward. Conversations are regrouped from the earliest change; the handover's history (spans of negative first page) stays beside the phone's spans.

post.description: An owner's grouping edit, idempotent by its id: split, merge, undo (of an earlier edit) or a dismissed split suggestion. Conversations are regrouped from where it applies.

400.description: An undo of an undo, or a split or merge inside an imported recording

404.description: An undo of an edit the server doesn't have
